NAME: User Browsing Profiles
DESC:
The recommendation team wants a compact profile per user, built from product-page views: which categories the user looked at, and in which order.

Implement solve so that it returns one row per user.

Input

views_df

column type description
user_id string never null
viewed_at string format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss; may be null
category string free text with inconsistent case and spaces; may be null

Rules

  1. category is normalized by trimming leading and trailing spaces and converting to lowercase (spaces inside the value are kept).
  2. Views whose normalized category is null or empty, or whose viewed_at is null, are ignored. Users without any remaining view do not appear in the output.
  3. num_views is the number of remaining views of the user.
  4. categories is the list of distinct categories of the user, sorted alphabetically.
  5. journey is the list of the categories of all remaining views of the user (duplicates kept), in chronological order of viewed_at. Views with the same viewed_at are ordered by category alphabetically.

Output

A DataFrame with exactly these columns, in this order:

column type
user_id string
num_views long
categories array
journey array

Rows are sorted by user_id ascending.

Example

views_df

user_id viewed_at category
u1 2024-03-01 10:05:00 "Shoes"
u1 2024-03-01 10:00:00 " books "
u1 2024-03-01 10:10:00 "shoes"
u1 2024-03-01 10:07:00 null
u2 2024-03-02 09:00:00 "Toys"
u2 2024-03-02 08:00:00 "toys"
u3 2024-03-02 08:00:00 " "
u1 2024-03-01 10:20:00 "Garden"

Expected output

user_id num_views categories journey
u1 4 [books, garden, shoes] [books, shoes, shoes, garden]
u2 2 [toys] [toys, toys]

Function signature

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame

def solve(views_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    ...

Constraints

  • Use the PySpark DataFrame API. Do not convert to pandas, do not call collect() or toPandas() inside solve, and do not use Python UDFs.
  • views_df has up to 10^8 rows; a single user has at most 10^4 views.
  • The returned DataFrame may be empty; its columns and types must still match the specification.

from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(views_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    # write your code here
    return views_df
SOLUTION:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(views_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    # 1. Normalisation puis rejet des vues inutilisables.
    clean = (
        views_df
        .withColumn("category", F.lower(F.trim(F.col("category"))))
        .filter(F.col("category").isNotNull() & (F.col("category") != "")
                & F.col("viewed_at").isNotNull())
    )

    # 2. collect_list ne garantit AUCUN ordre : on collecte des structs (viewed_at, category)
    #    et on les trie avec sort_array (tri sur le 1er champ, puis le 2e en cas d'égalité).
    grouped = clean.groupBy("user_id").agg(
        F.count(F.lit(1)).alias("num_views"),
        F.sort_array(F.collect_set("category")).alias("categories"),
        F.sort_array(F.collect_list(F.struct("viewed_at", "category"))).alias("views"),
    )

    # 3. views.category extrait le champ de chaque struct : array<struct> -> array<string>.
    return (
        grouped
        .select("user_id", "num_views", "categories", F.col("views.category").alias("journey"))
        .orderBy("user_id")
    )
